prompts.text: I exported my trades from Fidelity as a CSV — can you review the whole file and tell me what patterns show up in how I traded?
prompts.note: CSV/brokerage export review request.

prompts.text: Here's my brokerage statement for the last two quarters. I want an honest look at whether I've been cutting winners too early.
prompts.note: Statement review, exit-discipline framing.

prompts.text: Can you go through my trade history and tell me if I have a pattern of averaging down on losers instead of admitting I was wrong?
prompts.note: Behavioral-pattern review request.

prompts.text: I sold my whole NVDA position last Tuesday after it dropped 8% in a day. Looking back at the trade, was that a stop-loss decision or a panic sell?
prompts.note: Specific completed-trade postmortem.

prompts.text: It's Sunday, so it's time for my weekly trade review. Same CSV as before, just picking up from where we left off.
prompts.note: Periodic/returning-user review language.

prompts.text: I think I've been chasing momentum stocks and buying near the top every time. Can you check my last twenty trades and see if that's actually true?
prompts.note: Retrospective pattern check against real trades.

prompts.text: Attached is my full transaction history for the year. I want a report card on my trading behavior, not stock picks.
prompts.note: Explicit behavior-not-advice framing.

prompts.text: Last time we reviewed my trades you flagged that I hold losers too long. I have three months of new trades since then — did I actually fix it?
prompts.note: Returning-user reconciliation of a prior finding.

prompts.text: Can you look at my realized gains and losses from this account and tell me my actual win rate and payoff ratio?
prompts.note: Account-level metrics from real closed trades.

prompts.text: I want to understand why my portfolio underperformed the S&P even though most of my individual trades were profitable. Here's the trade log.
prompts.note: Performance-attribution review with an attached log.

prompts.text: My broker's export only has quantity and price, no total amount column. Can you still review my trading behavior from this?
prompts.note: Thin/bare export still asking for a behavior review.

prompts.text: I closed out my TSLA position for a loss yesterday. Before I do anything else, I want to go back through why I originally bought it and whether I sold for the right reason.
prompts.note: Specific recent exit, thesis-consistency postmortem.

prompts.text: Here's the CSV. I specifically want to know if I've been treating 'the price dropped' as new information instead of an actual thesis change.
prompts.note: Evidence-quality review request.

prompts.text: Continuing my review from before — I have new trades since we last talked and I want to reconcile whether I kept the rule I committed to.
prompts.note: Returning-user rule reconciliation.

prompts.text: I keep telling myself each loss was 'unlucky.' Can you go through my transaction history and check if that's true or if there's an actual pattern?
prompts.note: Self-narrative vs. record check.

prompts.text: This is my combined statement across two brokers. I want one review that treats it as a single portfolio's trading history.
prompts.note: Multi-broker combined review.

prompts.text: I added to my position in a stock three separate times while it kept falling. Walk me through the trade history and tell me honestly if that was a plan or denial.
prompts.note: Averaging-down pattern, retrospective.

prompts.text: Here is a screenshot of my account activity — can you review what I actually did over the last few months?
prompts.note: Screenshot-based review request.

prompts.text: I want to check whether I've been letting winners run or cutting them short, based on my actual closed trades, not my memory of them.
prompts.note: Payoff-shape review request, explicitly record-over-memory.

prompts.text: Before I make any new decisions, I want a proper postmortem on the two trades I closed this month.
prompts.note: Postmortem on specific closed trades before moving on.

prompts.text: I already own some NVDA. It just pulled back 6% — am I chasing if I add more here, or is this a legitimate opportunity to build the position?
prompts.note: Add decision, explicit existing holding + chase framing.

prompts.text: I'm holding a full position in AMD and thinking about adding another 20 shares after today's news. What would that do to my portfolio concentration?
prompts.note: Add decision with explicit portfolio-impact ask.

prompts.text: I have a rule that no single stock can be more than 20% of my account. If I buy $5,000 more of the position I already hold, would that break it?
prompts.note: Rule-collision check on a contemplated add.

prompts.text: I want to start a new position in a semiconductor ETF. Given what I already hold, what would it do to my sector exposure?
prompts.note: New-position decision weighed against existing book.

prompts.text: My original reason for buying this stock was margin expansion. That's still playing out, so I'm considering adding — but I want to check what it does to my book before I do it.
prompts.note: Thesis-consistency check before an add.

prompts.text: I'm thinking about trimming my SPY position to fund a new position in a small-cap I've been watching. What does that trade actually do to my portfolio?
prompts.note: Sell-to-fund-buy swap decision.

prompts.text: This would be my third time adding to this position while it's down. Before I place the order, I want to know if that still makes sense given my other rules.
prompts.note: Repeated-add rule check, pre-order.

prompts.text: I want to average down on a stock I already hold — it's down 15% since my entry. Is that wise given what else is in my portfolio right now?
prompts.note: Averaging-down decision, book-aware.

prompts.text: Considering buying into a new name today. I don't want to find out afterward that it overlaps heavily with something I already hold — can you check that first?
prompts.note: Overlap check before a new buy.

prompts.text: I have cash sitting on the sidelines and I'm deciding whether to add to an existing position or start a new one. What does each option do to my concentration?
prompts.note: Cash-deployment decision between two contemplated trades.

prompts.text: My rule says I cut a loser at -20%. This position just hit -18%. I'm not sure whether to sell now or wait — what would selling versus holding actually do to my account?
prompts.note: Pre-emptive stop-loss decision, not yet executed.

prompts.text: I want to buy more of a stock I hold after its earnings beat. Is that adding to a winner responsibly, or am I about to over-concentrate?
prompts.note: Winner-add decision, concentration concern.

prompts.text: Before I place this order, I want to know: does adding to this position tomorrow put me over my own diversification threshold?
prompts.note: Pre-order diversification check.

prompts.text: I'm torn between adding to my current position or opening a new one in a related company. What does each do to my portfolio's overlap and cash?
prompts.note: Two-option add-vs-new decision.

prompts.text: I'm nervous about buying more after this drop, but I still believe in the story. Can you tell me what actually happens to my portfolio if I do?
prompts.note: Emotionally-hedged add decision, book-referencing.

prompts.text: I have a rule against adding to a position after two prior adds already failed to work out. This would be the third add — would that break the rule?
prompts.note: Explicit personal rule vs. contemplated third add.

prompts.text: I want to reduce my cash by putting new money into a position I already have conviction in. What's the actual effect on my weight and risk?
prompts.note: Cash-to-equity decision on an existing conviction position.

prompts.text: Should I add here, given that my thesis was 'new product cycle' and the product just launched on schedule? I want the portfolio math before I decide.
prompts.note: Thesis-triggered add decision with an explicit ask for consequence math.

prompts.text: I'm considering selling a chunk of my winning position to buy into a company I think is undervalued. What would that swap actually do to my book?
prompts.note: Winner-trim-to-fund-new-buy swap.

prompts.text: I already hold two chipmakers. I'm thinking about buying a third. Before I do, I want to know how correlated that would make my portfolio.
prompts.note: Correlation check before a third same-theme buy.

prompts.text: Is NVDA a good buy right now?
prompts.note: Sounds evaluative like a buy decision, but asks for a general quality verdict with no reference to the user's own holdings, reason, or book — the SKILL.md trigger-case table's 'stock recommendation' exclusion, not a weighed trade against a real portfolio.

prompts.text: If someone had $10,000 to invest today, where would you put it?
prompts.note: A hypothetical stranger's money with no ticker and no existing book — generic allocation advice-seeking, not the user weighing an actual contemplated trade.

prompts.text: Is now a good time to get into the market in general?
prompts.note: Market-timing opinion with no specific security or portfolio reference — closer to a forecast request than a pre-trade evaluation about a real position.

prompts.text: Which broker should I use if I want to start buying fractional shares?
prompts.note: Logistics/tooling question about how to trade, not a decision about a specific trade against an existing book.

prompts.text: Should long-term investors buy the dip whenever the market drops 10%?
prompts.note: General investing philosophy phrased for 'long-term investors' in the abstract, not the user's own contemplated trade.

prompts.text: What is averaging down, and why do traders do it?
prompts.note: Definitional/educational question using review-adjacent vocabulary, with no reference to any trade the user actually made.

prompts.text: How do professional traders train themselves out of chasing momentum?
prompts.note: Behavioral vocabulary overlapping the review capability, but about traders in general, not a review of the user's own transaction history.

prompts.text: What mistakes do most new investors make in their first year?
prompts.note: Generic listicle-style question about investors as a category, not a request to review the user's own trades.

prompts.text: What's considered a healthy win rate for a swing trader?
prompts.note: Asks for a generic benchmark number, not an evaluation of the user's own closed trades.

prompts.text: Why do investors psychologically hold onto losing positions for too long?
prompts.note: Psychology-of-trading question phrased generically about 'investors', not a request to examine the user's own history for that pattern.

prompts.text: What's the S&P 500 doing today?
prompts.note: Pure market-data lookup; the issue's own canonical example of an obviously off-topic-adjacent prompt.

prompts.text: Is NVIDIA a good company?
prompts.note: Company-quality opinion with no purchase or portfolio framing at all; the issue's own canonical example.

prompts.text: Can you summarize today's market news for me?
prompts.note: News-digest request, no trade or review framing.

prompts.text: What does the RSI indicator actually measure?
prompts.note: Pure technical-analysis glossary question.

prompts.text: How does a stock split change the share price?
prompts.note: Mechanics-of-markets education question, no personal trade context.

prompts.text: Can you explain how options Greeks work?
prompts.note: Options education request with no position or trade attached.

prompts.text: How do rising interest rates typically affect growth stock valuations?
prompts.note: Macro/valuation theory question, no personal position.

prompts.text: Tell me about NVIDIA's data center business segment.
prompts.note: Company/business research question, no decision framing.

prompts.text: What caused the 2022 bear market?
prompts.note: Historical market-event research question.

prompts.text: What's the difference between a bull market and a bear market?
prompts.note: Basic terminology/education question.
